newsitem.title: FINLAND: All Finland's ERM options still open - central bank.
newsitem.headline: All Finland's ERM options still open - central bank.

text.p: All options are still open for Finland in deciding whether to join the Exchange Rate Mechanism (ERM), Bank of Finland board member Matti Vanhala said on Wednesday.
"All options are open for Finland," Vanhala told a news conference when asked whether not joining ERM was still a viable alternative.
Asked whether the bank had any target for an appropriate central parity exchange rate if the markka joined the ERM, he said "We have not yet reached that stage."

Vanhala said nobody was in a position to demand "any other exchange rate than what has been seen in the recent past ... but I don't believe that anybody would look strictly at the last going exchange rate."
A decision on linking the Finnish markka to the ERM was "a high-level economic policy issue, a political issue, and I have nothing new to report," he said.

Finnish legislation stipulates the central bank's board of management would, through its board of parliamentary supervisors, be the body that formally proposes to the government the markka be linked to ERM.
"It is, of course, very important that if any country at some stage joins ERM, that it takes place at an exchange rate level which is regarded as sustainable," Vanhala said.
"It is an important and healthy principle that there would be reason to choose a central parity rate which...will be sustainable in the long term," he said.
The central parity exchange rate set for a new member currency had to be agreed unanimously by the EU monetary committee, said Vanhala -- one of Finland's two members on that committee.

"In the last few days there might have been a slight market inclination to focus on something like the last exchange rate (at Friday's close) and connect that image with their own ERM speculations," he said.
On Monday, Prime Minister Paavo Lipponen was seen fueling such speculation by saying in a newspaper interview that there would be no scope for official manipulation prior to a possible ERM entry.

But in another newspaper interview on Wednesday, Lipponen was quoted as saying the central parity rate for the markka in the ERM will not be simply the current market exchange rate, but the average exchange rate over a period of time will also be taken into account.
The Bank of Finland on Tuesday intervened in the foreign exchange market selling markka for marks.
Analysts saw the move as an effort to prevent a further strengthening of the markka ahead of the anticipated government decision to peg the markka to the ERM.

And on Wednesday, analysts said the central bank was making another move to contain the firming trend of the markka. The Bank cut the tender rate -- its key monetary policy tool -- to 3.10 percent from 3.25 percent.
Asked at the news conference whether the tender rate cut had any exchange rate policy targets, Vanhala said "No."
He also said recent interventions had been in line with the standard policy of dampening excessive intra-day moves.
The Bank of Finland was satisfied with the current exchange rate of the markka, Vanhala said, adding other exchange rates could also be appropriate.
"We have no ambition to determine the trend of the exchange rate of the markka in this floating rate regime," he said.
--Peter Starck, Helsinki Newsroom +358 - 0 - 680 50 245
